How Chameleons Really Change Colour

It isn't pigment. It's tiny crystals, and the lizards tune them like an instrument.

By Ada Lovelizard · 20 October 2026

For centuries people assumed chameleons changed colour the way an octopus does, by spreading and gathering pigment in their skin. That turns out to be only a small part of the story, and in the most dramatic species, it is barely a part at all.

In 2015 a team in Geneva showed that panther chameleons carry a lattice of guanine nanocrystals in a layer of skin cells called iridophores. When the animal is calm, the crystals sit close together and reflect blue light; when it is excited, the lattice swells, the spacing grows, and the reflected colour slides toward yellow and red.

FacebookTwitterEmailCopy link

Combine that structural blue with the yellow pigment sitting above it and you get the vivid greens of a resting male. Stretch the lattice and the same skin flashes orange. Nothing has moved but the spacing between crystals, a few hundred nanometres at most.

Researchers describe it less like paint and more like a tunable optical filter. The animal does not choose a colour from a palette; it adjusts a physical structure, and colour is the side effect. That is why the shifts can be so fast, sometimes under a minute from one end of the range to the other.

A second, deeper layer of iridophores has larger, more disordered crystals. It reflects much of the near-infrared, and scientists think it may help the lizards manage heat, which matters for an animal that cannot make its own.

So why change colour at all? Camouflage is the popular answer, but most of the dramatic displays happen in plain view: males flushing bright to warn rivals, females darkening to refuse a suitor. Colour, for a chameleon, is mostly a way of talking.

Did you know chameleons were optical engineers?

0 votes

There is still plenty that isn't understood. Nobody yet knows exactly how the cells swell and shrink the lattice on command, or how the nervous system coordinates it across the whole body so smoothly.
